questions.passage: In Faraday's account, the candle wick is not simply a thread that happens to burn. Melted fuel rises through its fine spaces by capillary action, much as water enters a towel. The flame supplies the heat that melts the solid fuel, while the wick delivers the resulting liquid to the region where it can vaporize. Thus, the continued operation of an ordinary candle depends on several processes sustaining one another, rather than on the combustion of an isolated piece of string.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the central idea?
choices: A candle's sustained burning depends on interacting processes that move and transform its fuel.
A candle's wick supplies most of the energy released as its surrounding fuel melts.
Capillary action becomes effective only after a candle's liquid fuel has vaporized.
The resemblance between a wick and a towel establishes that both materials burn similarly.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Плавление, подъём жидкости и испарение поддерживают горение совместно.

B — неверно: Текст не называет нить главным источником энергии.

C — неверно: Капиллярный подъём относится к жидкости до испарения.

D — неверно: Аналогия объясняет впитывание, а не сходство горения.

questions.passage:
Text 1
A divided sense of identity is best addressed as a private problem of inconsistent preferences. Public judgments need not enter its explanation.

Text 2
Self-awareness can be shaped by persistent judgments imposed by a devaluing society. An internal conflict may therefore have a source that cannot be located solely in private preference.
questions.stem: Which issue is most central to the disagreement?
choices: Whether people can ever have more than one preference.
Whether all public judgments are favorable.
Whether social evaluation can help produce what is experienced as an inward conflict.
Whether an identity can be described in written language.
questions.explanation:

B — неверно: Такого тезиса ни один текст не защищает.

C — верно: Разногласие касается социальной причины внутреннего опыта.

D — неверно: Возможность описания не оспаривается.

It makes the grounds of one's own judgment answerable to the actual disagreement rather than to a conveniently simplified substitute.

questions.passage: The opening world of Pride and Prejudice is full of confident judgments about other people's intentions. Families interpret arrivals, invitations, and manners through expectations about marriage and status. The narrative's irony allows such judgments to be heard without requiring the reader to accept them as neutral descriptions. What a community confidently calls obvious can therefore reveal the community's priorities as much as it reveals the intentions of the person being discussed.

A community can know a newcomer's intentions only if it has no shared expectations.

questions.passage: A bright candle flame can appear to be a uniformly burning mass. A flame's visible outline therefore conceals internal differences that a simple observation of its silhouette would not disclose.

It identifies a historical explanation that the author defends against Faraday's findings.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Faraday compares a candle's combustion with processes occurring in animal respiration.
• The comparison concerns transformations of materials, including the production of carbon dioxide, rather than a claim that lungs contain a visible flame.
• By linking an everyday object to a living process, he broadens the reach of the chemical explanation.
• Its usefulness depends on the specific similarities identified, not on treating candles and animals as identical in every respect.
questions.stem: The student wants to state both the usefulness and the limit of Faraday's analogy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Faraday discusses both living animals and an ordinary household candle.
Animals and candles have obvious differences in their outward appearance.
Respiration and candle combustion can be compared through chemical transformations without claiming that animals literally contain candle flames.
Carbon dioxide is mentioned in the discussion of material transformations.

Every familiar object contains hidden water that heat merely releases unchanged.

questions.passage: Mill worries about custom becoming a final authority rather than a source of experience that people may examine. questions.stem: What does the third sentence accomplish?
choices: It prevents the critique of unquestionable custom from being mistaken for a rejection of historical experience.
It establishes that past practices have never yielded any useful information.
It introduces a chronological account of one particular custom's origin.
It reverses the claim that inquiry should remain open.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Оговорка отделяет критическое использование прошлого от отказа от него.

B — неверно: Полезность опыта прямо допускается.

His knowledge does not operate in an empty social space. The narrative complicates a simple opposition between a brilliant individual and an ignorant town: even a reformer must act through institutions and relationships that can both enable and constrain the reform. Intellectual purpose alone does not determine how a career develops.
questions.stem: What does the phrase 'an empty social space' help emphasize?
choices: That knowledge affects action within a network of relationships rather than under socially neutral conditions.
That the town contains no institutions through which a physician could work.
That scientific inquiry is absent from Lydgate's ambitions.
That the narrator considers all relationships equally unimportant.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Образ подчёркивает неизолированность знания.

B — неверно: Институты прямо названы значимыми.

C — неверно: Научная мотивация указана в первом предложении.

The collected water resembles water obtained from a nearby tap.
The candle is shorter after burning than it was before the experiment.
A wet candle is more difficult to light than an otherwise similar dry candle.

questions.passage: Darwin distinguishes the occurrence of variation from the preservation of particular variations by breeders. A breeder need not have caused a useful difference in order to increase its prevalence by choosing which organisms reproduce. This distinction separates the origin of an available difference from a process that changes how common it becomes. An account of selective breeding is therefore incomplete if it assumes that every characteristic favored by a breeder must first have been deliberately produced by that breeder.
questions.stem: Which distinction is central to the text?
choices: Causing a variation and increasing its frequency through reproductive choices are different processes.
A breeder can preserve a variation only by directly causing its first appearance.
Every variation becomes more common regardless of which organisms reproduce.
Deliberately choosing parents prevents any inherited characteristic from changing in frequency.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Происхождение различия отделено от его распространения отбором.

B — неверно: Это именно отвергаемое допущение.

C — неверно: Репродуктивный выбор влияет на частоту.

D — неверно: Текст говорит о возможном увеличении частоты.

The appearance of a dwelling is the only concern motivating Dorothea's interest.
A generous reforming aim deserves recognition while still requiring practical knowledge to become effective.
Enthusiasm alone guarantees that every proposed improvement will work as intended.

A trait appears and disappears before any organism carrying it can reproduce.

Every bird changes in the same way immediately after hearing a breeder's instruction.

questions.passage: A candle burning beneath a closed vessel eventually goes out. This result alone might tempt an observer to say that any enclosed space prevents burning. Yet the relevant feature is not enclosure considered in isolation: the flame changes the available air, and the supply is not renewed. Faraday's demonstrations direct attention to the material conditions of combustion. The shape of the vessel is less informative than whether the surroundings can continue to provide what the reaction requires.
questions.stem: Which claim best states the main idea?
choices: The effect of enclosure should be explained through the changing supply of materials needed for combustion.
The vessel's shape is sufficient to predict exactly how long any candle will burn.
A candle extinguishes as soon as any object is placed anywhere above it.
Enclosure affects a flame without producing any change in the surrounding air.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Замкнутость действует через условия снабжения реакции.

B — неверно: Форма названа менее информативной, точного прогноза нет.

questions.passage: Darwin warns that the struggle for existence should be understood broadly. A plant at the edge of a desert may depend on moisture rather than engage in visible combat with another plant. Survival also depends on relationships with other organisms and on producing offspring. Reading it only as a description of direct fighting would exclude many of the conditions that the argument treats as relevant to the persistence of a population.
questions.stem: Which choice best captures the main idea?
choices: Plants encounter no struggle because they cannot engage in physical combat.
Reproduction is unrelated to whether a population persists.
The struggle for existence includes environmental and reproductive dependencies beyond direct physical conflict.
Only competition between members of different species can influence survival.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Пример растения расширяет понятие борьбы.

B — неверно: Потомство включено в релевантные зависимости.

C — верно: Термин охватывает условия сохранения, а не только схватку.

A candle's extinction establishes that no gas remains anywhere inside its vessel.

Replacing a vessel with an identical one necessarily restores the original air supply.

questions.passage: A classification can group organisms by a conspicuous shared feature, but such a feature need not be the best guide to their relationships. Similar ways of living may favor similar structures in different lineages. Darwin's discussion instead gives weight to patterns of affinity interpreted through descent. A useful classificatory character may consequently be one whose significance is not obvious from its immediate practical function. The most visually striking resemblance and the most informative resemblance need not coincide.
questions.stem: Which statement best conveys the main point?
choices: Every organism with a similar way of living must belong to the same immediate lineage.
A character becomes irrelevant to classification whenever its practical function is unclear.
The value of a resemblance for classification depends on what it reveals about relationships, not simply on its conspicuousness.
The most striking resemblance always provides the most reliable evidence of descent.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Сходные условия могут действовать в разных линиях.

B — неверно: Неочевидность функции не исключает ценности для классификации.

C — верно: Диагностическая значимость отличается от заметности признака.

D — неверно: Совпадение этих критериев не гарантировано.

Faraday examined a sample from the flame's interior.
a sample from the flame's interior was available for examination.
the narrow tube's usefulness became apparent during the experiment.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Внутренняя область не является тем, кто проводит пар трубкой.

B — верно: Подлежащее Faraday является действующим лицом drawing.

questions.stem: Which evidence would most weaken an argument based only on a shared conspicuous structure?

The structure is easy for observers to notice without special equipment.
The structure performs a useful function in both of the organisms being compared.

produce
bend under
postpone

questions.passage: Darwin considers not only the physical conditions on islands but also the means by which organisms could reach them. A habitat may appear suitable for a group that is nevertheless absent because crossing the intervening sea presents a barrier. Distribution therefore records opportunities for arrival as well as opportunities for survival after arrival. An explanation confined to present-day climate would miss a historical condition that can help account for differences between otherwise comparable places.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea?
choices: An organism's absence from a suitable habitat may reflect limits on reaching it rather than inability to survive there.
Present-day climate fully explains every difference between island populations.
Organisms that cross a sea must necessarily survive in every habitat they reach.
Any two islands with similar weather must contain identical groups of organisms.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Пригодность среды и возможность расселения — разные условия.

B — неверно: Климатического объяснения недостаточно.

C — неверно: Прибытие и дальнейшее выживание не тождественны.

D — неверно: История прибытия может различаться.

Two islands differ in both climate and all known opportunities for arrival.

A map uses the same color for islands with similar average annual temperatures.

A reason to ignore the history of all island populations.
A claim that all remote islands are equally unsuitable for life.
Two different names for exactly the same ecological event.
